title: Lights and vessels: the soul in the body, sight in the eye, and the 248 limbs of the King
overview:
Before he can explain the lights of *Zeir Anpin* and its unions, the Mitteler Rebbe opens a five-chapter introduction on lights and vessels. The lights of the *sefiros* are *b'li ma*: real, but not definable, the way you know a person and still cannot say who he is. The vessels are a tangible, defined expression, and through them G-d is revealed to man and conducts a world that seems separate. The four spellings of the Name, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, all speak of the vessels.

The body is the *mashal*: brain, heart and liver for *neshama*, *ruach* and *nefesh*; every vessel an inside, middle and outside; 248 limbs of the King. Light in a vessel is like sight in the eye. It changes its nature, from spiritual to physical, and it is limited, as the hand can lift only so much, though a sudden fright shows the soul's power has no limit. Yet the matter is made to fit the form, from its lowest level, like a cup designed from the wish to drink, and so body and soul grow together, day by day, until seventy.

terms.gloss: vessels: the tangible, defined expression of something, like the body for the soul or words for an idea
sefiros without a what: as lights they have no mahus, real but not definable
garments: the ten vessels G-d made to reveal Himself to man and to conduct the world
the spelling out of a letter's name: the yud, alef or hei in between that make the four Names
three rulers: the brain, the heart and the liver, the vessels of neshama, ruach and nefesh
head, middle and end: the inside of a vessel that serves its purpose, the middle that is the vessel itself, the outside by which it is used
the body of the King: the kelim of Zeir Anpin, with their 248 limbs
garments: Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya as the clothes of the body, or thought, speech and action
a change of nature: a spiritual consciousness becoming a physical, measurable process
limitation: the measure the matter of the vessel imposes on the light
matter and form: the matter limits the form, yet is made to fit it
thickening: making an abstract goal more and more tangible until it becomes the form of a vessel

blocks.text:
Until now the Mitteler Rebbe explained, only a little bit, the lights of *Abba* and *Ima* (lit. father and mother), the *partzufim* (statures) of *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding), and the way they join together, on the inner level or the external level. There are three different levels of *yichudim* (unions): they can connect in *chachma*, *bina* and *daas*, in *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, or in *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*. And before that he explained the lights of *Abba* and *Ima* themselves: the way they receive from the *mazalos*, from the arms, and from the *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod* of *Keser*.

Now we ought to be moving right along on to *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance), whose *partzuf* is called both *Yisrael* and *Yaakov*. Why it has both names will be explained later.

Once the lights of *Zeir Anpin* are explained, the *yichudim* of *Zeir Anpin* with *Nukva* (lit. the female) have to be explained, the union of *Yisrael* and *Leah* or of *Yaakov* and *Rachel*. Later he will say that there are really four combinations: *Yisrael* with *Leah* and with *Rachel*, and *Yaakov* with *Leah* and with *Rachel*, and all of them have to be explained.

But that is a long way off. Now begins a five-chapter introduction about lights and vessels. Then he will explain *Zeir Anpin* generally a little, give a recap of *yichud*, explain the difference between *Yaakov* and *Rachel*, and only then the *yichudim*. It is five chapters before he talks about *Zeir Anpin* specifically again, and ten chapters before the *yichudim* of *Zeir Anpin* with *Nukva*.

blocks.text:
But first we have to understand some prerequisite concepts about lights and vessels, in general and in their details.

It is a very famous saying of the *Zohar*: "He and His life forces are one, He and His organs are one." It is a *mashal* (analogy) of the soul and the body: He is one with the soul, and He is one with the body. *Garmohi* means organs, the body. So the life, the soul, means the lights of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), and the organs, the body, are a *mashal* for the vessels. Now he is going to explain how the body is a *mashal* for the vessels.

phrases.he: ומצד בחינת האורות דעשר ספירות בכלל ובפרט
phrases.en: When we're talking about the lights of the ten *sefiros* in general and also for each *sefira*,
then we call the *sefiros* *b'li ma*,
that they are *b'li mahus*, that they don't have a *mahus*, which means that you can't tell me what they are.
like it says,

phrases.he: ולאו מכל אינון מדות כלל כו'

blocks.text: From the side of the lights of the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), in general and in each *sefira*, they are called *sefiros b'li ma* (sefiros without a what), *b'li mahus*: they have no *mahus* (what a thing is in itself). You cannot tell me what they are. They are not tangible or defined; they do not have a defined existence; they could really be anything. It is the vessel that makes it something limited and defined.

blocks.title: The birthday present
blocks.text: Back in chapters 10 and 11, where he first mentions *b'li ma*, he says it is like *Echad*. You want to buy somebody a present for his birthday. You already know the general *ratzon* (will): you want to buy a present. But you do not know yet what to get him. What is it? "I don't know." You do not know, because it is still just the general light.

**Like it says**, "And He is not any of these *middos* at all." The light is the revelation of G-d, and **G-d has nothing to do with any of these *middos* at all**; He is really above them all. So the revelation of G-d within the *sefiros* is not definable. Only the vessel defines it. Then we can call it wisdom: wisdom is the vessel, and what is revealed in it is that He is wise, "the wise guy, the one who is wise." But the thing you know about Him from the wisdom is not a tangible thing; the way He is expressed is not really definable.

blocks.title: Who are you?
blocks.text:
Say that you see Him in the wisdom. You can get to know Him a little from His wisdom, from His kindness, from all these different things. But what you get to know is not a tangible thing.

Like, I know you, as much as I know you, after all of our experiences together and sitting next to you in 770. But if somebody asks me, "Who are you?" I still cannot explain your *etzem* (essence). "It's just you, it's just Shmuel." It is not something tangible, even though I see you in all kinds of things. I can even sometimes say, "Oh, I can see you in it. That's a you kind of thing." There is a certain style. That is the revelation of the person, and it is *b'li ma*: it is not tangible, and the vessel is.

Like a friend you know, as much as you know him, after all your experiences together. If somebody asks you, "Who is he?" you still cannot explain his *etzem* (essence). "It's just him." It is not something tangible, even though you see him in all kinds of things. You can even say, "Oh, I can see him in it. That's a him kind of thing." There is a certain style. That is the revelation of the person, and it is *b'li ma*: it is not tangible, and the vessel is.

blocks.text: You know the way a person is, but you know it through what he does, what he thinks, and what he says. And just because something is *b'li ma* does not mean that it is not a real thing, or that you do not know it at all. "That's not what it means at all." It is the real thing, like a person's talent: you can appreciate a person's talent for something, and that is still like a light, still a *b'li ma* thing.

blocks.title: A home, not a house
blocks.text: Or you want something that is not yet defined. You want a home. You do not want a house yet; you just want a home. That is a *ratzon*, and it is not a fake thing. It is a real thing; that is the real *ratzon*.

These are the kind of things philosophers bother themselves with: "What is love?" "What is truth?" They do not want just particular examples of it; they want the light, the real thing.

And there are different levels of light. There is the regular light, and even that is *b'li ma*, and there is the *etzem or* (the essential light). It does not have to be the revelation of the person, which is like the *etzem or*. Even the light of the *sefira* itself, the real light of *chachma*, is still *b'li ma*.

What is the real thing of wisdom? You do not really see it. You see it in particular instances, but the essence of wisdom is not a tangible thing; you cannot really define it. It is a human thing, that you recognize these things.

Kindness, for example, is not something you could write down on paper: if you do this and you do that, you are being kind. It depends on the situation. It is a certain sensitivity, an attitude of wanting to do good, not a defined thing yet. And the same with wisdom and understanding: all these things of intellect are what you feel is graceful and beautiful and symmetrical and logical and orderly.

blocks.question: What is a working definition of *or*?
blocks.text: Start with a definition of *kli* (vessel), because that is a lot easier: it has a *ma*. A *kli* is a tangible, defined expression of something. The *or* (light) is the abstract, intangible point behind it. It could be the goal, or it could be what the tangible thing represents, because the tangible thing is always representing something. The intangible thing it represents is called a light.

blocks.question: Is it the difference between *chachma* and *bina*?
blocks.text: Kind of. *Chachma* is often called *or*, and *bina* puts things into *osios* (letters) of *machshava* (thought), which are like *kelim* (vessels). So in a way it is that relationship, but it is really a more general thing. It is true that it says *chachma* does not have *osios* and *bina* has *osios*, but really *chachma* also has *osios*, just a higher type. *Chachma* also has a *kli*, but it is not like a language. You are not thinking to yourself in a language in *chachma*; you are just picturing things. The letters of *chachma* are the particular way you think about whatever you are thinking about.

blocks.title: The car you picture
blocks.text: If you are thinking about a car, you imagine a certain car. That particular car you chose to imagine is a *kli*, because you are using it to represent all cars. So a higher level of *kli* can be abstract to a lower level.

This is how the words of a teacher become the inner understanding of the students: to them it is like the light, but to the teacher it is the vessels. Really, though, it is not true there. His words are like a *masach* (screen); the light is *boke'a* (breaks through) it and comes through from it. His words themselves are not the actual light. They just carry the light.

The *kli* also has *pnimiyus* (an inner side) and *chitzoniyus* (an outer side). The *or* is more *pnimiyus*: the *or* is the soul, and the vessel is the body. Everything has a soul. That is in a way a better definition: someone in an art form, or someone speaking, can be going through the motions but not have the soul. Some people do things technically right, but they do not have the talent, the feeling, the sensitivity. Those are the soul; that is like the light.

A lot of times people learn things, parrot back what they learned and pass their tests, but they just really do not get it. "They really don't." They have the vessels, the letters, but they do not have the light. On the other hand, a person who *chaps* it (grasps it) and really gets the light, even if he does not do so well on the test, memorizing and whatever, actually gets it: he can apply it, explain it and use it. "If you have the light, it's a real thing."

blocks.title: Gemara in Chassidus terms
blocks.text:
Sometimes, Rabbi Walters says, he has this problem: you understand something, you have the soul, but you do not say it in the language the other person is used to, the right terminology. Each culture has its own jargon. Even within Chabad, Chassidic people, *baalei nigleh* (scholars of the revealed Torah) and people who are into *Chassidus* each have their own.

He was learning with a *baal nigleh*, and to explain the *Gemara* he would use *Chassidus* terms, like the *chomer* and the *tzura* (the matter and the form). It used to really annoy the man; he did not get what Rabbi Walters was talking about, and it bothered him until he got used to it, because it was not said in the right terms. There is a lot of truth to that: sometimes a very big thing is just saying things in people's words. "You got to know the lingo." The *kelim* are the words.

blocks.title: Getting married
blocks.text:
So it is important: even if you have the light, it is not enough. You can understand something, but if you want to bring it over to somebody else, a lot of times the *kelim* are very important.

It is like when you want to get married. The person's personality, character traits, beliefs, ideas and views are like the soul, and the way they look is their body: how old they are, how tall, what they look like. People also care about the body, "or *nit* (not)?" If you have everything good in the soul but do not present it in a way people like, they are not necessarily going to take it. Some people will, some people won't; some care more about the body, some less.

then the *sefiros* are a tangible existence. We can say what they are.
and this is what it says,

blocks.text: So the lights are not tangible. **But when we speak about the *kelim* of the *sefiros*, then the *sefiros* are a tangible existence. We can say what they are.**

**And this is what it says** in the *Zohar*: **G-d made ten garments**, ten *tikunim* (a *tikun* means a garment), **and He called them ten *sefiros*.** G-d made these ten vessels to reveal His abilities through, and their purpose is to reveal Himself to man, and to conduct the world with them. Through these ten, G-d is revealed in a way that we can know Him in a tangible way.

That is the thing of putting something into a vessel: then you are able to express it to somebody separate from you. Whenever you want to express something to someone separate, you have to put it into a vessel; if you want to express ideas, for example, you have to speak. And these are the interface of the *hishtalshelus* as *Hashem* set it up: G-d relates to the world through them.

Why? Because this is what allows the world to seem separate: it is conducted only through these vessels. For example, G-d decided to reveal Himself through the *chesed* (kindness) of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation), which is the idea of creation: He decided to reveal Himself as a creator, and that is of the light. The vessel, the idea of being able to create, gives our world the meaning of a created entity that seems separate. And now that is connected to G-d, because it is a revelation of G-d's ability to create. So it is the intermediary between something separate and Him: the world, which seems separate and limited, is connected to Him by the vessels of the *sefiros*, because He chose to reveal Himself through them.

The *sefiros*, as he will explain, are in between. In one way they are limited and in one way they are infinite, and so they can be the intermediary that reveals the connection between the world and G-d. We are not saying that G-d had to use the *sefiros* to make the world. But since *Hashem* wanted to make the world so that it seems separate from Him, and that through working we find Him, He made it in steps, and one of the steps is the *sefiros*.

He could have revealed Himself in infinite other ways, but He chose these. And these are tangible things, so we can know what it means to create something. The real thing of that ability, in a way, we do not know, because we do not have the ability to create something from nothing; but we can at least have a *hasagas hametzius* (a grasp that it exists) of it. Actual creation we actually know. We see the creation and understand that there is an ability to create behind it, and from that we know that there is a creator. So we see G-d through creation; that is the way it reveals Him to us.

And the world is conducted through them. Your soul is too spiritual to move a physical thing; it has to come into your body, and through your hand it moves a physical thing. Really, G-d could just do what He wants. But for the world to be conducted in a way that it seems like a world, it has to work through limited systems, things that make it seem to have a certain nature and certain inherent limitations.

"Cuz it would blow the cover if G-d would just be doing whatever He wants without some sort of order." So G-d runs the world with a certain system and certain attributes. Even miracles, things above nature, look like a normal miracle. We know what to expect: if we are going to have a classical biblical miracle here, we know what it is going to look like. That is because of the vessels of *Atzilus*: the miracle vessel looks a certain way. That is what makes the world a world, that it goes through these limitations.

sections.title: The four Names are the vessels of the sefiros
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called the four spellings of G-d's Name, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, and together the secret of the Holy Name. All of this, names and numbers, speaks of the vessels.

blocks.text: And this is also the idea that the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called the four names: 72, 63, 45 and 52. The name *Havaya* can be spelled out in different ways. The letter *yud* is always spelled *yud-vav-dalet*. But the letter *hei* can be spelled three ways, *hei-yud*, *hei-hei* or *hei-alef*, and the letter *vav* can be spelled *vav-yud-vav*, *vav-vav* or *vav-alef-vav*. There are four combinations of those that we talk about all the time.

*Ayin Beis* (seventy-two), the name of 72, is spelled with the *yuds*: *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-yud*, *vav-yud-vav*, *hei-yud*. Added together, the numerical value of all those letters is 72, and it corresponds to *chachma*. *SaG*, the name of 63, is spelled the same way, except that the *vav* is *vav-alef-vav*: instead of a *yud*, which is ten, it has an *alef*, which is one, so it is nine less, 63. It represents *bina*.

*MaH*, the name of 45, has *alefs*, *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-alef*, *vav-alef-vav*, *hei-alef*, and represents *Zeir Anpin*. And *BaN*, the name of 52, is spelled with *heis*: *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-hei*, *vav-vav*, *hei-hei*, really just the letters being doubled. It represents *Malchus*, as is known.

"I'll tell you the truth": Rabbi Walters never saw much of an explanation of why. *Kabbala* uses two *meshalim*: the soul and the body, and letters. This whole thing of the *miluim* (spellings out) and the spellings of names is the *mashal* of letters. *Chassidus* explains a lot about the *mashal* of the soul and the body, the psychology and everything; that is the main thing here in *Shaar HaYichud*. But the details of the *mashal* of the letters and the spellings he does not see explained much, and he says he does not understand that system that well. He thinks he knows the general idea of why, but he did not see a clear explanation, so he is trying to figure it out.

The *yud* represents the point of *chachma*, and that is why the *milui* of *yuds* is in *chachma*. The *alef* has a *yud* on top, a *yud* on the bottom and a line in between: a point being revealed through a *masach*. There is a *bekia* (breaking through) of the point, as if it comes through an interface and is revealed in a different way.

So in *bina*, he guesses, you still see the point on the level of *chachma*, intellectually, but now the *middos* of it are given an interface, a definition: you are breaking up the *middos* of the idea. And in *Zeir Anpin* everything is interface, because the *middos* really come from *chachma* but go through *bina*, and now the entire *chachma* has been interfaced into a *midda*.

And the idea of *Malchus* is that it gives over the *etzem*, but *b'helem* (in hiding); the whole *etzem* actually comes over. That is why the letters are just doubled. This is explained in *Likkutei Torah* on, he thinks, *Chayei Sarah*, the first discourse, about the *Me'aras HaMachpela* (the doubled cave): *Malchus* is called *Me'aras HaMachpela* because of the idea of doubling, and that is the name *BaN*, whose letters are doubled, *hei hei*, *vav vav*, *hei hei*. It explains there that the *etzem* comes over exactly the way it is. So it is doubled without a *memutza* (a middle): there is nothing in between, the *etzem* comes over straight, like *yesh me'yesh* (something from something).

blocks.title: Giving a dollar, giving an idea
blocks.text:
If I give you a dollar, there is nothing in between: I give it to you and you get it. But in spiritual things, ideas and emotions, when I give you an idea, it is not that you get it exactly the way I have it. There is a *tzimtzum* (contraction), and it comes through as a light that just represents it. You have to extract the point I am trying to make and read between the lines. I give you an example, and you have to extrapolate the general principle. In spiritual things you do not get the *etzem*; that is the idea of *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing).

That is why there is either a *yud* in between, which is like a *tzimtzum*, or an *alef* in between, a different type of *tzimtzum*. That is the point behind those *miluim*: in *chachma* you get the *nekuda* (point) as it is, and in *bina* and in *Zeir Anpin* the point comes through an interface, like a *masach*.

blocks.text: **In the terminology of the *Zohar*, the whole idea of the ten *sefiros* is called the secret of the Holy Name**, and all of it is only from the side of the vessels. All these places that speak about the names and the *gematrios* (numerical values) are the idea of the vessels of the *sefiros*. The name of 72 is the vessel of *chachma*.

Which level the names refer to depends on the context; they could refer to any level of the *hishtalshelus*. Usually, whenever you talk about anything without specifying, you are talking about *Atzilus*, because that is where the main action goes on. That is the main center, because *Atzilus* is like the soul in the body.

blocks.title: Saying a person's name
blocks.text: Take you. If I say "Shmuel", people picture you: your body with your consciousness in it. Unless I specify that I am talking about your inner subconscious, your inner self the way it is detached from your body, or about the expression of you in your work, which would be like *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, I am talking about you, and that is *Atzilus*, the center.

If it is talking about the way we see G-dliness in creation, then it is talking about *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and it will say "the *chachma* of *Beriya*": the way we see G-d's wisdom in creation. But if you just say *chachma*, you think right away of G-d's power of wisdom the way it is in the vessel of wisdom, *chachma* of *Atzilus*. I could be talking about G-d's inherent potential for wisdom before it comes into the vessel, or the way it is higher than what we call wisdom, but then I have to specify it, or the context has to mean it.

sections.title: Three rulers: brain, heart and liver for neshama, ruach and nefesh
sections.summary: The three main systems of the body are the vessels of the three levels of the soul: intellect in the brain, emotion in the heart, biological life in the liver. *Chaya* and *yechida* are above the limitation of vessels.

phrases.en: The explanation of these matters is known, the idea of the lights and the vessels,
on the teaching of the *Zohar*:
there are three chiefs above, there are three supernal rulers, leaders:
the brain, the heart and the liver, and so on,
which are the three vessels for the *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama*.
The *neshama*, which is the intellectual part of your soul, goes into your brain.
The *ruach*, which is an emotional part of your soul, goes in the heart.
And the *nefesh*, which means just biological life, is in the liver.

blocks.text: The explanation of these matters, the lights and the vessels, is known from the teaching of the *Zohar*: there are *tlas shlitin* (three rulers) above, the brain, the heart and the liver. In a person's body the three main systems, not really organs, are called the brain, the heart and the liver: the nervous system, the cardiovascular system and the digestive system. Those are the three vessels for the *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*.

So the three levels of the soul that come into consciousness in your body are *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*, and they go into the general vessels of the brain, the heart and the liver. The *neshama*, the intellectual part of your soul, goes into your brain. "Do I need to explain that? You think with your brain." The *ruach*, the emotional part of your soul, goes into the heart; for those who do not know why the emotions are in the heart, that will be explained.

That is kind of common knowledge. But scientists like to say it is ridiculous, because they don't know; and not just scientists, everybody. "The modern men like to make themselves feel good by making ancient cultures seem stupid." They take the old ideas, build them into the most ridiculous construct, and then laugh at it. "It's a straw man defense. It's really ridiculous what they do." They never consider that maybe the ancients meant something more intelligent than what they make of it.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks scientists and "the modern men" as making ancient cultures seem stupid with a straw man.
sensitivity.publishable: That is kind of common knowledge, though it is often dismissed today: the old idea is built into the most ridiculous construct and then laughed at, without considering that maybe the ancients meant something more intelligent than what is made of it.

blocks.text: So the emotions are in the heart, and the *nefesh*, which means just biological life, is in the liver, because your liver is what makes you live: it digests your food for you. That is what you need. You do not need your brain for biological life.

blocks.title: What a person can live without
blocks.text:
In medicine, he says, there are three vital organs that a person dies without if they fail for some minutes, depending on which one: the liver, the heart and the kidneys. He thinks the kidneys are the least vital, that a person can live 15 minutes without kidneys, and the heart for like 5 minutes; how long the liver, he does not remember.

But a person does not need a brain to live at all, for physical life. You could put a person on machines, and he does not really need the brain, "in a way they do, but basically they don't." You need it for consciousness, not to be a living thing, biologically alive like plants are alive; "that's what they call him a vegetable." Just to go through the process of life, using energy and expelling waste, you do not need the brain.

sensitivity.reason: Medical claims given from memory and partly wrong: which organs are the vital ones and how many minutes a person survives without each. His point that the brain is needed for consciousness and not for biological life is kept.
sensitivity.publishable: A person does not need the brain for physical life as such. You need it for consciousness, not to be a living thing, biologically alive the way plants are alive. Just to go through the process of life, using energy and expelling waste, is not what the brain is for.

blocks.text: The main function of life does not happen in the heart; it happens in the liver. The main thing of life is using energy, which is digestion. The heart just passes that energy along to the other organs and adds oxygen to it so they can burn it. It helps the digestive system "spread the wealth", but the main function happens in the liver.

blocks.title: The liver takes the poison apart
blocks.text:
They can make an artificial heart, but they cannot make an artificial liver. In a way the liver is the smartest part of your body; its function is ridiculously complicated. Everything that goes into your body and into your bloodstream goes into the liver: what you eat, when you drink alcohol, when you smoke a cigarette, if you do drugs, if you inhale car fumes. The liver takes it all apart into basic molecules and atoms and puts it back together into useful things, and any poison it alters molecularly so that it is not dangerous, and passes it out of the body.

The liver is so good at that, he says, that you can drink alcohol and use drugs and not die right away, though they are poisons and should really kill you. A person is harmed by them eventually only because sometimes a small percentage, less than 1%, stays behind and damages the liver and the body, or because there is so much at one time that the liver cannot get rid of all of it.

sensitivity.reason: Says the liver is why one can drink and use drugs "and not die right away", with a percentage of harm given from memory; a reader could take it as reassurance about alcohol and drugs.
sensitivity.publishable: They can make an artificial heart, but they cannot make an artificial liver. In a way the liver is the smartest part of your body; its function is very complicated. Everything that goes into the body and the bloodstream goes into the liver. It takes it all apart into basic molecules and atoms and puts it back together into useful things, and what is poisonous it alters so that it is not dangerous, and passes it out of the body.

blocks.title: It takes a lot of brains to make a body
blocks.text:
The liver is also the only organ that can regenerate: unless a lot of it is damaged, it fixes itself up, and you can live with only about 25% of it. It has to be seriously damaged to affect a person's life. And what it does, taking food and everything apart and putting it back together into the right amino acids, proteins and sugars that the body needs, basically builds your body from scratch. "The liver is the brain of the physical body's operation." Science cannot duplicate it at all; it would be really difficult and expensive.

They cannot duplicate the brain, because it is consciousness, and you need a soul for that. But its physical function is like a computer, a bunch of wires connected, and they can kind of duplicate that. "It's not easy to make a body. Takes a lot of brains to make a body." These are the organs that are the centers for these different aspects of the soul.

phrases.en: But the *chaya*, *yechida*
does not come into the vessels; they do not have a particular organ center.

blocks.text: **But the *chaya*, *yechida* does not come into the vessels; they do not have a particular organ center.** The *chaya* is like the inner will and volition, and all that goes along with it, and it is in the whole body equally. The *yechida* (the essence of the soul) is your inner self, which is also in your whole body equally. Neither of them is limited to any particular vessel.

There are physical things that are kind of vessels for the *chaya* and *yechida*. The *kruma d'avira* (the membrane of air) is like a vessel for the *chaya*, because that is where the senses come from, and the liquid, it says, is like a vessel for the *yechida*, or some say the skull. But first of all, they are not revealed in it. The brain is set up in a way that makes sense for it to be the vessel for thinking, because it is like a computer; the *kruma d'avira* is not set up like that. It is not really a proper vessel; it is just *shoreh* (rests) on it, it is just *makif* (encompassing) on it.

Also, those things go over the whole body; they are not centralized. The liquid goes through the whole body and does not just stay over the brain. Even the *kruma d'avira* goes over the whole brain, and he thinks there is such a thing over the whole spine, and other parts of the body may have similar things; it could be that this too is not so central. But they definitely do not limit it. They are just the vehicles it is expressed through in the body, not vessels that limit it, because it is not in them in a *pnimiyus* way. This will be explained.

sections.title: Inside, middle and outside: the 248 limbs of the King and His garments
sections.summary: Every vessel has an inside that serves its purpose, a middle that is the vessel itself, and an outside by which it is used. Nine *sefiros* of nine, times three, plus the five *chassadim*, make the 248 limbs of *Zeir Anpin*, the body of the King; beyond the body are the garments.

phrases.en: And the vessels:
it's composed of head, middle and an end; beginning, middle and end; an inside, middle and an outside,
which is the inner part of the vessel,
the middle of the vessel,
the external part of the vessel.

blocks.text: Now he is just introducing all the basic concepts of vessels. There are the main vessels, the brain, the heart and the liver, the vessels for the *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*. Then there are the *chaya* and *yechida*, which do not have real vessels, in the way of *hislabshus* (being enclothed), actually being in the vessel. And then every vessel has three aspects: **head, middle and an end**, beginning, middle and end, **an inside, middle and an outside**: **the inner part of the vessel, the middle of the vessel, the external part of the vessel.**

blocks.title: The cup
blocks.text: As is known, it is like a cup. There is the inside of the cup, the space in the middle, where it holds the liquid. There is the outside of the cup, where you hold it. And there is the actual body of it, the actual stuff it is made of, which is the middle. In a way these are the same thing and in a way not. The real vessel itself is the middle. The inside is just part of the shape of the vessel: it is made in a way that it can hold something, which is its purpose. And the outside is where you are able to hold it, so that you can use it.

blocks.title: The handle and the blade
blocks.text:
Some cups have a separate handle; that is called the external vessel. It does not help the cup at all, it just helps you hold it. Sometimes the outside has a special grip or a special handle, and sometimes not. And sometimes the inside, the part that does the function, is a special thing, like a knife with a special blade. Then there is the main body, which just gives it stability or value, and then the handle.

So the inner part of the vessel is where it serves the purpose, which is the higher thing of it. The middle is the actual vessel itself, with its properties. And the outside is what allows it to be used.

blocks.title: The arm
blocks.text: This will all be explained later, so it can be said shortly here. Take your arm. Its inner part is the way it is connected to the power of movement, through the nerves that connect it to the brain, so that your soul can tell it what to do. The middle part is the arm itself, the way it is constructed, with muscles built to let it move in certain ways. And the external part is the way it is able to move and grab things and do things, the way it relates to things outside of you.

In a way it says this of the *basar*, *gidim* and *atzamos* (flesh, sinews and bones): there are the bones, the tendons and connecting things like the veins, and the meat. The meat is like the external vessel: it is what actually does the movement. The tendons connect the bones in the right way so that they can move the right way; the blood vessels carry blood and oxygen to give it the energy to move; the bone is what makes it able to do it; and the nerves tell it to do it.

phrases.en: It's known about the 248 limbs of the king:

phrases.he: דט׳ ספירות של בחינת זעיר אנפין
phrases.en: the nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*,
Nine times nine, 81,
has really three parts to it,
the inside, middle and the outside.
So three times 81 is 243.
And when you add the five *chassadim* that make the body grow, you get 248.

blocks.text: It is known about the 248 limbs of the King. Why do we say 248 limbs? That is the number of limbs. If you count the bones in the body, he thinks you have to count cartilage too, like the kneecaps, something like that, and it is 248. But what is the *cheshbon* (count) of the *sefiros*? It comes from the *sefiros*, and here we are talking about upstairs: the nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*, nine because it is not *Malchus*, have 248 limbs. Why?

Nine times nine is 81, because each of the nine *sefiros* has nine *sefiros* to it, since it is a *partzuf*; it is only *Zeir Anpin*, without *Malchus*. *Nukva* is its own *partzuf*. It starts off having ten, but the *Malchus* of each *sefira* is broken off through the *nesira* (the sawing apart), which will be discussed later. Like *Adam* and *Chava* ("we just had *Parshas Bereishis*"): they were originally made with two faces, and then she was cut off from him and built into her own *partzuf*. So *Zeir Anpin* starts off with *Nukva* attached and then it is cut off: the *Malchus* of each *sefira* is cut off and built into *Malchus*, its own *partzuf*. Now it has nine *sefiros* left, and each has only nine. So nine times nine, 81.

The nine general *sefiros* correspond to nine general organs, as it says in *Pasach Eliyahu*: the right side of the brain is *chachma*, the left side is *bina*, the skull is *Keser*; then the right arm, the left arm, the torso, the right leg, the left leg and the reproductive organ. Those are the nine *sefiros*. And each of those really has nine: your arm has the upper arm, the middle arm and all of your fingers. It is not just one thing, it is a lot of things.

And each one of those, say just your upper arm, really has three parts, *rosh toch sof* (head, middle and end), the inside, the middle and the outside. There is your skin, your muscle, your veins and nerves, and your bone, all different layers, and in general we divide it into three. So three times 81 is 243. And now we add five: **when you add the five *chassadim* that make the body grow, you get 248.** That is the *cheshbon* of 248.

Usually the five *chassadim* (kindnesses) mean the liquids that make the body grow. It could be that in this context it means not the liquids but the ends of the bones that grow, or something; Rabbi Walters says he is not sure what the Mitteler Rebbe means here in the body by the five *chassadim*.

phrases.he: והוא כללות ענין כלים דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: is the general idea of the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*,
which is called the body of the King.

blocks.text:
Now he is going to tell all about the human body, because that is the *mashal* for the *kelim* of *Atzilus*. The *kelim* of *Atzilus* are what is called the body, the *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King), so he will talk about all the different aspects of the body and how they work, and get into all this physiology.

This **is the general idea of the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*, which is called the body of the King.** These are the vessels of the ten *sefiros*: each vessel has nine, each of those has three, and then there are the five *chassadim*, so you have 248 limbs. And, as was said, these are the idea of the names. The *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) will come in the next chapter; this is the general *mashal*.

phrases.en: So too, *Hashem* made *levushim* for Himself. He made garments,
So these *levushim*, the *mashal* for that is like *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh*.
We'll explain all of this.

blocks.text: **So too, *Hashem* made *levushim* for Himself. He made garments**, and the *mashal* for that is the garments we wear: a shirt and pants and a hat. As it says, there are two main *meshalim* in *Kabbala*, and one is the soul and the body. The worlds before *Atzilus* are like the soul, *Atzilus* is like the body, and *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* are like the clothes: the hat, the clothes for the head, is *Beriya*; *Yetzira* is like the clothes for the body, a shirt and a coat; and *Asiya* is like the pants and shoes, the clothes for the lower part of the body.

It also speaks of *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh* (thought, speech and action), which is what it says here, a less *megusham* (physical) *mashal*. Recently in *Tanya*, at the end of the last letter they were learning, the Alter Rebbe says that to understand these things properly you have to know how to take the teachings of the Arizal away from their *gashmiyus* (physicality), their metaphoric connotations. They are written in a very physical way, and you have to figure out the *nimshal*. So these *levushim* (garments) are thought, speech and action, and all of it will be explained.

sections.title: Light in a vessel, like sight in the eye: first, a change of nature
sections.summary: The general model of light and vessel is the soul's power of sight in the eye. The first thing that happens is *shinui hamahus*: a spiritual consciousness becomes a physical process, as intellect in the brain, movement in the body and growth in the plant.

phrases.en: However,

phrases.he: הנה ענין אור וכלי דרך כלל,
phrases.en: now we're going to explain the idea of the light and vessel in general.

phrases.he: הגם שיש בו הרבה אופנים שונים מאד,
phrases.en: Although there are many different types of lights and vessels and ways that they work,

phrases.he: אך כללותו הוא על דרך אור וחיות הרוחני של ראיה רוחנית
phrases.en: the general *mashal* for it is like the spiritual power of consciousness of sight, of vision, the soul's power to see,

phrases.he: כשמתלבש וממוזג בהגשמה בכלי חומר העין
phrases.en: which then is enclothed into the eye, into the physical matter of the eye,
physical sight.
So here there are two components, there's two aspects to this eye-soul thing going on here.

blocks.text: **Now we're going to explain the idea of the light and vessel in general.** There are many different types of lights and vessels and ways they work, but the general *mashal* is the soul's power to see, which is enclothed in the physical matter of the eye. The matter of the eye is *memuzag* (mixed), put together in a way that it is able to see: it is clear, it has little nerves receptive to light, with chemical reactions, the cones and the rods and the retina and all that. So the eye becomes a physical tool for seeing. The eye is the *kli*, the vessel or the tool, for the soul's power of sight.

The consciousness is not a physical thing. The actual consciousness of sights and perceptions is not physical at all; it is spiritual. There is no physical existence of red and blue; those are psychophysical, as was discussed before. Those are the light and the *chayus*, and *chayus* means consciousness. And the eye is the vessel of physical sight.

blocks.title: How the eye sees
blocks.text: So they have biological, physical sight, and they can explain how the light hits the lens, which inverts the image and projects it on the back of the eye through this clear liquid, and the retina has nerves with cones and rods, receptive to different brightnesses of light and different colors. That is why your eye has only a certain resolution: there are only about 288 sensors per millimeter or something, so you can only see with a certain amount of definition. There are certain physical limitations to the way it works.
**So here there are two components** to this: when your power of sight goes into your physical eye, two things are happening.

phrases.en: The first thing is
it's now changing its nature from a spiritual consciousness to a biological process.
That physical sight can see physical things.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ברוחניות אור הראיה
phrases.en: On the other hand, it's not so with the spiritual power of sight.

blocks.text: **The first thing is** *shinui hamahus* (a change of nature) from spiritual to physical: **it's now changing its nature from a spiritual consciousness to a biological process**, a physical biological process that scientists and doctors can measure and describe. They will explain to you how it works, that there are chemicals sensitive to light that trigger different things. There is a whole thing how it works.

"They only tell half the story. Of course they only tell half the story." Sometimes they try to make it out to be the whole story, as if it explains everything, but it really does not explain why you see blue. They can explain that blue triggers this chemical reaction and yellow triggers that one, that your eye is receptive to these different pigments, and there is something to it. But why in the end you see blue as blue is not a physical thing. There is no way they can explain biologically or scientifically why it should look the way it does. That is totally coming from your soul.

**Physical sight can see physical things**, and it is something measurable by physical means. It goes both ways: the whole process, both how it sees and what it sees, relates to the physical world. So now you can see cups and bowls and trees and clouds, and say exactly what is going on. **On the other hand, it's not so with the spiritual power of sight.** The soul's consciousness does not let it see physical things without the eye. It is just aware of itself.

phrases.en: So too with all the other powers of the soul, like, for example, the power of intellect,
which goes into the vessel of the brain,
until you can actually call it what we know as thinking, intellectualizing, coming up with ideas.

blocks.text: So too with all the other powers of the soul, like the power of intellect, which goes into the vessel of the brain. The brain is set up to be able to think; it is like a computer. It has all these nerves, and electrochemical impulses can follow all different types of patterns, and each pattern can represent a different thing; depending on how you order the patterns, they can represent all different types of thoughts. And it has chemicals, released by certain patterns or stored up to trigger certain patterns, and that is how memory works and how things are associated. It is a very complicated vessel, a good vessel for thinking, physically. But the actual understanding is not in the brain; it is in your soul. "And that's why no matter how good of a computer they make, it will never have consciousness."

**Until you can actually call it what we know as thinking**, *hischakmus*: coming up with ideas, the process of insight and understanding, study, which is really the way it works in the physical brain. Just as with sight the light has to go into your eye and trigger a reaction before you see, so the brain works in a certain way: you get a certain stimulus, and you analyze it and make patterns and associations. That is what we right away associate with studying or thinking.

phrases.en: And the power of movement,
when it comes out physically in your body,
And the same thing with the power of growth, the spiritual power of growth,

phrases.he: שמורכב ומלובש בצמיחה גשמית בגשם הצומח
phrases.en: which then goes into the physical power of growth, which is a whole physical, chemical, biological process.

blocks.text: **And the power of movement**: your soul has the power of movement spiritually, but **when it comes out physically in your body**, it depends on the way the human body is built. It can only move in certain ways and has a certain range of motion. We are not built the same way as flies: flies can fly and cling to walls, and we can't; we can't turn our head around backwards. So it becomes limited to our limbs, but it becomes physical, and now we can make a physical movement. The soul cannot move physically. Its movement is a spiritual concept: it connects itself to something. The soul can choose to connect itself to whatever it wants and direct its consciousness to that thing.

blocks.question: Could you fly with a human soul?
blocks.text: Sure, why not? We do not have the same soul as flies, we have a human soul, but as far as the power of movement goes, we are the same. That is why *Chassidus* says a *gilgul* (reincarnation) is painful: a human soul cannot express itself in the body of something other than a human. It cannot think, it cannot use its creative abilities, its emotions cannot be expressed properly, so it feels trapped.

blocks.title: A human soul in a fly
blocks.text:
The fly does not have the power of thinking like a person, in its soul, and its vessel corresponds to it; the vessel fits. The human body is made to be a fitting vessel for the human soul, and a fly's body is not. "You could stick a human soul in the fly's body and it would work, but it would be very annoying." It is like using a butter knife as a screwdriver: you could do it, but it is frustrating, because the tool does not give you the ability. The soul is what actually has the ability; the body is just what lets it express it.

The power of movement is not really different for flying than for walking. But human intellect is a certain type of power that flies do not have: creative introspection, philosophical inquiry, they do not have that in their soul. With a human brain "they would be a really smart fly", but it would not be like a person.

And that is a question of what soul it is. That is the thing of *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man): once the soul goes through *Adam Kadmon*, the soul itself gets a certain form, a human soul or a fly's soul, so it is not able to go into any body. Before that, every soul is the same on that level. That is the idea of *nishmas kol chai*, the soul of everything.
That is the one aspect of the vessel: the light changes and becomes something that can relate to physical things, because the soul cannot relate to the physical world.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 44 opens by summing up the first aspect, the change of nature, before it reads line 32.

blocks.text: **And the same thing with the power of growth**: the spiritual power of growth goes into the physical power of growth, **a whole physical, chemical, biological process**. There are chemical reactions, little bacteria that take the nutrients apart and make them into different things, and a whole thing of how it works with the light and the chlorophyll, photosynthesis.

We do and we do not know the spiritual power. That is the whole point of what he explains in chapter 1: you cannot get the depth without the length and the width. You always have to start with the length, because the length is where it is brought down into a *mashal*, an example that is practical and tangible, that you can actually know. You cannot give over the light, the depth, directly, because it is abstract; it is *b'li mahus*. So you give a particular, physical, tangible example, and from it extrapolate the light.

So we do know what the idea of intellect is, and of seeing; we understand the spiritual concept behind them, but by seeing it in particular examples. We understand growth as separate from the process that makes it work, because it could work differently. If it grew differently, instead of working the way it works, "Well, so what? What do we care?" It does not have to be like that, theoretically. The physical process is just a means, a tool that allows growth to exist. The carbon and the light, the nitrogen, the water, the oxygen and the carbon dioxide are really irrelevant; that is not the real thing of growth. The real thing of growth is something that builds itself and multiplies itself and makes itself bigger.

blocks.title: Why does a tree grow?
blocks.text:
The way the world works now, yes, all that would make something grow. But there are two questions. When you see a tree growing, where does it think it is going? Why is it growing? They can explain the whole physical thing of how it grows, the light and whatever, but why is it growing? There is an inherent *ratzon* that makes it want to grow. That is what they call *teva* (nature): a *ratzon* higher than reason and knowledge, that for no reason wants to do that. That property is not physical. It is a spiritual soul, a certain drive enclothed in the physical world that becomes the nature of the physical world, and that nature has no physical explanation.

"Whenever they say nature, that's what they mean": a spiritual thing beyond the physical world, which they have no explanation for; it is just the way it is. And they do not realize the philosophical implications of that word. "Science doesn't tell you why, it just tells you how."

But the main point is that it becomes physical growth, because the concept of growth will not actually grow particular plants, but the physical power of growth will. That is the one *inyan* (matter): it goes from being spiritual to physical, it changes its *mahus*, from a spiritual entity to a physical entity.

sections.title: Second, the vessel limits and measures the light
sections.summary: The second thing a vessel does is limit: physical sight reaches only so far, the brain can hold only so much, the hand can lift only so much. The spiritual power itself has no limit, as a sudden fright shows.

phrases.en: The second thing that goes on when the light goes into the vessel
when it goes into the vessel, the vessel has certain limitations that it imposes on the power, on this light. So now it is limited according to a certain way, as measured.
It's like physical sight:
you can only see up to 60 miles.

blocks.text: **The second thing that goes on when the light goes into the vessel** is the *hagbala* (limitation) and measure in the matter of the vessel: **the vessel has certain limitations that it imposes on the power, on this light.** Now it is limited in a certain way, measured. **It's like physical sight: you can only see up to 60 miles.**

blocks.question: What does it mean that you can only see up to 60 miles? I can see the stars and the Sun, much farther away, and from a high enough mountain you can see farther than 60 miles.
blocks.text:
Rabbi Walters is not sure exactly. It probably has something to do with what was said about the eye having only a certain number of sensors, and so only so much definition: if something is far enough away, for a given size, the light from it falls between the sensors and you won't see it at all.

"Oh, no." What he thinks he figured out is that the Mitteler Rebbe means the maximum depth perception you can have. Anything beyond a certain distance seems flat, like the horizon, a backdrop; you cannot tell which mountain is farther away. You tell depth by the distance between your two eyes and a couple of other tricks, and when something is far enough away they stop working. The Sun and the Moon look like they are the same distance away. So it could be that you cannot see something as being farther than 60 miles away. The main thing is that there are physical limitations to the power of sight.

Exactly what limitation he is talking about, it does not say explicitly, so one can only try to figure it out. But that is the point: look in science books or ask doctors about physical sight, and they will tell you all its limitations. Your eye is receptive to only a very narrow wavelength of light; visible light is a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum. You can see only certain colors and certain brightnesses. And your eye takes a picture only every sixteenth of a second or something, because every time light hits your eye it triggers a chemical reaction that makes you see, and it takes time to reset to be able to see again. There are all these kinds of limitations.

phrases.he: וכן ענין התחכמות ותנועת הגשם, מתפשטים בהגבלה מצומצמת
phrases.en: So too with your intellect and your movement, that when they become in the physical vessel of your body, they are limited.
They are specifically very limited.
And then there's a certain point where they will fail, your ability was used up.

phrases.he: כמו שתקצר גשם השגת כלי המוח
phrases.en: Like sometimes your brain just can't understand,
and its ability will just be used up because the vessel is not big enough.

blocks.text: **So too with your intellect and your movement**: in the physical vessel of your body **they are limited**, *davka* (specifically) very limited, **and then there's a certain point where they will fail**; your ability is used up. **Sometimes your brain just can't understand**, and its ability is used up **because the vessel is not big enough.**

You have to develop your brain. It is like a muscle: you exercise it and it becomes better at thinking. There is a point where an idea is too complicated for the brain and it cannot handle it; you have to exercise your brain to make it finer, sensitive enough to handle it. Or there is too much information for it to handle at once; your brain can deal with only so much information at one time. And then there is how long you can think for, your attention span. These are actually physical things.

Little kids do not have as much brain capacity as someone older, and the more a person develops certain parts of his brain, the better he gets in that area; it is a physical thing. And a person can actually hurt himself if he does not rest his brain and thinks too hard. Rabbi Walters does not know the technical medical term, but they can kind of have a nervous breakdown or whatever, "and like kind of fry their brain", if they push it too hard. And every now and then your brain needs to rest and sleep and do different things to reset.

sensitivity.reason: A medical claim he says he cannot name (thinking too hard can cause "a nervous breakdown" and "fry their brain"), close to advice a reader might act on.
sensitivity.publishable: Little kids do not have as much brain capacity as someone older, and the more a person develops certain parts of his brain, the better he gets in that area; it is a physical thing. And every now and then your brain needs to rest and sleep and do different things to reset.

phrases.he: וכן יוקטן ויופסק כח תנועה הגשמית שמכח היד, בפעולה או בהגבהת משאוי וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: So too, your power of movement is too small sometimes, and it will stop: when you're doing something, eventually your hand gets tired or just can't do it, or something is too heavy for it to lift, and you just can't do it.

blocks.text: **So too, your power of movement is too small sometimes, and it will stop**: your hand gets tired, or something is too heavy to lift. It is too small. This is because of the limits of the moving power. There are ways you just cannot move, and you have only a certain amount of strength; you can move it only so fast and only so hard. There are different limitations.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן מצד עצם כח הרוחני של המניע התנועה,
phrases.en: On the other hand, this actual spiritual power of movement
does not have any limitation, and it will never stop, will never run out.

phrases.he: וראיה מהגבהת משא כבד הבא בבהלה פתאומית, ביתר הרבה מכחו,
phrases.en: And the proof for this is when a person has a sudden scare, and they lift something that's much heavier than they could really lift,
which is because of the *makif*: the soul forces the body to do more than it can really do.

blocks.text: **On the other hand, this actual spiritual power of movement does not have any limitation, and it will never stop, will never run out.** The proof is when a person has a sudden scare and lifts something much heavier than he could really lift: the *makif* (encompassing light) of the soul forces the body to do more than it can really do. There, in a way, the essential power of movement is revealed.

blocks.title: Feats in a fright
blocks.text: Exactly how that works, he does not know. But there are all these stories of people who did crazy things, jumped over huge things a person normally could not jump over, in wars and such, or even fit themselves into spaces too small for them, as if they shrank their body a little to fit in somewhere. Normally that is not within the ability of the body.

What happens is that the soul has much greater control over the body than is normally revealed, and it forces the body to comply with its *ratzon*, like a miracle, and the physical body really could do it. He explains later the source of miracles, that it comes from the level of the *makif*. The actual matter is stupid and does not care. Water does not really care whether it flows or stands up like a wall, as when the sea split; it is just stuff, and it will do whatever it is told. So the matter of your body will do whatever the soul tells it. Normally the soul cannot tell it to do certain things, but when it is in big trouble and so has a huge *ratzon*, it reveals this essential ability, like a miracle on the body.

It depends on how high you go: the deeper you go, the more limitations are lifted. If you would reveal deep enough, you could really do anything. You see this even with hypnosis, where there are different levels of how deep you can bring somebody into his subconscious, and the deeper you go, the more amazing things you can get him to do.

blocks.title: Faith healing and placebo
blocks.text:
And there are deeper and deeper levels. This is also why, by the way, a lot of things like faith healing work: at a certain level of your soul you have the ability to heal yourself, to make your body fix itself and work however the soul wants. A person who is sick, he says, is sick because the soul kind of stopped caring and let the body deteriorate; but if you tap into a deeper level, the soul can make the body fix itself, and the deeper you go the more miraculous things it can do, even instantaneously.

There is placebo, and there is even more than placebo: people go to some psychic healer, or some spiritual guy tells them something, and because they believe in him so much it can actually do something, but only because they believe in it. Really all stuff has an element of that. Even regular medicine is not guaranteed to have a certain effect; your body reacts to the stimulus in a way that comes from your soul, not purely physically. There are levels of how much it is *meluvash b'teva* (enclothed in nature), but either way it is within nature, and either way it is really above nature. It depends how far you want to go.

sensitivity.reason: Says faith healing and psychic healers work, that a sick person is sick because his soul stopped caring, and that regular medicine is not guaranteed; a reader might act on it about medical treatment.
sensitivity.publishable: And there are deeper and deeper levels, at which the soul has more power over the body than is normally revealed. Even the way the body reacts to a stimulus comes from the soul, not purely from the physical. There are levels of how much it is *meluvash b'teva* (enclothed in nature), but either way it is within nature, and either way it is really above nature.

sections.title: Matter and form: the matter fits the form, made from its lowest level
sections.summary: Matter both changes the form's nature and limits it, yet it is made to fit the form: the vessel comes from the thickening of the spiritual form, from its lowest level, as the design of a cup comes from the wish to drink. So the lowest level of growth, life, intellect and sight goes into the plant, the blood, the brain and the eye.

phrases.he: וכך הוא כל ענין חומר וצורה
phrases.en: This is the whole idea of a *chomer* and a *tzura*.

phrases.he: שהחומר, מלבד שהוא בא בשינוי המהות,
phrases.en: Besides that when you put it into matter, it changes from spiritual to physical,
it also limits the form.

blocks.text: **This is the whole idea of a *chomer* and a *tzura***, *chomer v'tzura* (matter and form): the matter limits the form. Whenever you put something into a form, it limits it. Besides that it changes from spiritual to physical, **it also limits the form.** It represents something, but now it is limited. Take the idea of a cup: if you make a cup, you have only one particular example of a cup, though really you can make different cups. It is always limited.

phrases.he: אבל החומר הוא מעין ודוגמת הצורה,
phrases.en: But nevertheless, the matter is made in a way that is according to the form, so it fits the form,
like the vessel, the eye: the matter of the eye is actually built in a way that's good for seeing,
and the vessel of the mind is made, the brain is made like a computer.

blocks.text: **But nevertheless, the matter is made in a way that is according to the form, so it fits the form.** The cup actually is a cup, made to be a cup. The matter of the eye is actually built in a way that is good for seeing; it has to be clear. When they make a video camera they have to make it kind of like the eye, or it won't work; it has to be made in a certain way to be a vessel for that. **And the vessel of the mind** is made like a computer, in a way that fits thinking.

phrases.he: אבל החומר נעשה מהתעבות והגשמה של הצורה הרוחנית,
phrases.en: Because the matter is made, not the actual stuff, but the form of the matter is made from the thickening and the materializing of the spiritual form,
from the lowest levels of the spiritual form comes the physical form.

blocks.text: **The matter is made, not the actual stuff, but the form of the matter is made from the thickening and the materializing of the spiritual form.** You have the concept of what you want to accomplish, which is abstract; you make it more tangible, you thicken it and make it physical, and you come up with a physical form, the form of the vessel. For example, your desire to drink water is the form of the cup.

blocks.title: Designing a cup
blocks.text: From that desire you figure out, based on the situation and the way water works, that you need something that can hold water. Certain materials can hold water and certain cannot; it cannot have holes in it. So the shape and the material of the cup are already starting to become defined, partially materialized in your mind: you are looking for something watertight and practical to use as a cup. Then you want a way to hold on to it, so you need some sort of handle, or the outside has to be like a handle. Looking at the goal, an abstract thing, within the limitations of the world around you, you start to get a picture of the way the cup should be. Then you add aesthetic considerations, that it should match your kitchen, and you get a pretty good idea of what you are looking for.

blocks.title: The mug and the wine glass
blocks.text: Then it depends what you want it for, hot or cold. A mug is good for hot things, because ceramic insulates; a glass is not so good for hot things, because the outside gets very hot, and it can ruin the glass. And wine glasses are made for wine: the stem is there so you do not heat up the wine by holding the glass and do not get the glass dirty with your hands, so you can see the color of the wine and how clear it is, and keep it a little chilled. So the form of the cup is made according to the light, the *ratzon* you are trying to accomplish, and the matter is made to be a tool according to the specifications you need.

But there is a difference between abstract considerations and practical, circumstantial ones. It is like going back to chapter 15, or the difference between a house and a home: it goes from an inner desire to a *ratzon murkav* (a composite will). That is what it means that from the *hisabus* (thickening) of the light comes the vessel. The form of the eye is made to fit the power of sight: the power of sight has certain specifications, and so within the physical world, the way it works, the eye has to be clear or it won't work, it has to be sensitive to light. That defines how the eye has to be built in order to work.

**From the lowest levels of the spiritual form comes the physical form.** You have to make it more and more particular and more and more tangible, until it is finally particular enough that you can make an actual physical thing to fulfill that purpose, as was just described.

phrases.en: So, for example, from the lowest levels of the spiritual concept of growth,
that becomes the source of the physical growth.

phrases.he: וכמו סוף של חיות הרוחני דנפש, מלובש בדם,
phrases.en: or like the lowest level of the consciousness of the soul goes into the blood,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב כי הדם הוא הנפש כו'
phrases.en: like it says, that the blood is the soul.

blocks.text: **For example, from the lowest levels of the spiritual concept of growth**: the spiritual concept of growth exists on much more abstract levels than plants growing from dirt. But its most practical, tangible kind, a concept of growth that can relate to physical growth in the ground, **becomes the source of the physical growth.** For it to work it has to go in a certain form, and that is why the physical growth has a certain form.

**Or like the lowest level of the consciousness of the soul goes into the blood**, the power of movement goes into the blood, **like it says, that the blood is the soul.** Only the part of your soul that can be revealed in the energy of your body, the desire for movement, the power of movement and all these things, is there, and it is only the most external and most defined application of the spiritual idea of movement.

phrases.he: וכך סוף המדריגה של אור השכל הרוחני מתמזג בחומר כלי המוח,
phrases.en: And the same thing with the lowest level of intellect that can go into the brain,

phrases.he: וכן סוף הגשמה דרוחניות הראיה ממוזג בחומר העין
phrases.en: and the lowest level of sight goes into the eye.

blocks.text: **And the same thing with the lowest level of intellect that can go into the brain, and the lowest level of sight goes into the eye**, because the actual spiritual ability, the actual consciousness, does not go into the body. The brain does not actually have the consciousness of thinking or the creative ability. It is just that the spiritual power has a certain form, so those specifications are represented in the physical form. But that is only its most external parts, the ones that can have a physical representation; the more spiritual parts stay in the realm of spirit.

sections.title: Body and soul grow together, day by day until seventy
sections.summary: The matter grows with the form: the body becomes a better vessel as the soul's powers mature, and using a power makes the body grow for it. Both take time, day by day, until full maturity at seventy, which is why the Torah sets ages and why one stands up for the old.

phrases.en: Therefore we find

phrases.he: שבכל מקום באין הגדלת החומר עם הגדלת הצורה כאחד ממש
phrases.en: that the body and the soul grow together.

phrases.he: כמו בהגדלת חומר כלי הגוף, שנגדלים ביחד עם גידול אור וחיות הצורה הרוחניות,
phrases.en: Like the body: as you get older, your body grows and develops, at the same time you mature emotionally, intellectually, and your strength gets bigger.

phrases.he: כמו גידול הכנת חומר המוח לפי ערך גידול האור והצורה של השכל,
phrases.en: Like the development of the brain according to the development of intellect,

phrases.he: שכאשר יגדל התינוק ויצמח אור שכלו ברוחניותו, ממילא יצמח כלי הכנת מוחו
phrases.en: as a child grows and develops mentally, matures, at the same time the brain matures physically.

blocks.text: **Therefore we find that the body and the soul grow together.** As your body develops physically, your spiritual powers develop; they always go together. **As you get older, your body grows and develops, at the same time you mature emotionally, intellectually, and your strength gets bigger.** It is not a coincidence; it has to be. When the body grows, it is becoming a better vessel. The *or* is there, but the vessel needs to become better so that it can hold the light better.

But it works both ways. As the body develops it can hold more light, and also, when you use your body more, if you exercise, you get stronger and your muscles grow. The more you use a certain power, the more it shows that you have a *ratzon* for it, and you bring that light in, and that makes your body a better vessel for it. Every time you do something with your body, your soul shines a certain light into it, and that refines your body to be a better vessel for that light; the more you do a certain thing, the more your body builds itself to conform to that light.

That is why if you exercise a lot your body gets stronger, though only in the type of exercise you do, and if you think a lot you get smarter in the kind of things you think about. Your body is really just simple matter, and it conforms to whatever desire your soul expresses through it, to be as good a vessel as it can for that form. So the body develops a certain amount on its own, which opens you up to greater potential, and the more you push yourself, the more it develops.

**Like the development of the brain according to the development of intellect**: **as a child grows and develops mentally, matures, at the same time the brain matures physically.** And it works both ways: there is a physical process of the brain maturing, and also, as you start to think more, your brain develops more.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ימים ידברו ורוב שנים כו'
phrases.en: that days speak and many years bring,

phrases.he: שנגדל הכלי עם האור יום יום עד ע' שנה,
phrases.en: that every single day the vessel develops along with the light, and they both develop together until at 70 years old

phrases.he: שבא לכלל גדלות המוחין כידוע ודי למבין:
phrases.en: you reach complete intellectual maturity, and the brain is completely physically mature also.

blocks.text: As it says, **days speak and many years bring**, he thinks, *de'ah* (knowledge), or something like that: just going through life, you develop more and your abilities develop more. That is both because your body develops physically and because you use it more, and it goes hand in hand. **Every single day the vessel develops along with the light** until at 70 years old you reach complete intellectual maturity, and the brain is completely mature physically too. And that is just the brain; there are other things too.

If someone had used his brain more, maybe he would be better. But no matter how much you think, it takes time, and this is why the Torah has set ages: *bar mitzva*, 20, six for *chinuch* (education), nine. It does not matter if you are a *Rebbe*, really smart and really mature physically and spiritually: you are still not *bar mitzva* until 13. And even at 13, if you don't have two hairs, you are not *bar mitzva*, because you need both to be that mature. You have to have gone through so many days, because every single day more of your soul comes out. There is something that happens just from the passage of time, regardless of your effort: you experience more things and see more situations, and without any effort on your part you have to mature every day, just from the process of life. That is the way G-d set it up. And if there is a problem with the body, so that it is not yet a proper vessel, like a boy who does not have two hairs yet, he is not *bar mitzva* either; and if he has two hairs before *bar mitzva*, he is not *bar mitzva*, because you need the time. You need both together for full maturity.

If you put in effort you will be more mature, but only within what can be accomplished by that age. A 20-year-old is never going to have the same depth of maturity as a 70-year-old. There is something you gain with age, which is why according to the Torah you stand up for somebody old, even someone who is not Jewish, even someone who is not smart. An elderly person has something just from experiencing so much life: he feels the essence of things more. That is the idea of the *or* and the *kli*: the passage of time brings in more light, and as it does, the body develops too. You need both.

reviewQuestions.question: What does it mean that the lights of the *sefiros* are *b'li ma*, and why does that not mean they are not real? Use the example of knowing a person.
Why did G-d reveal Himself and conduct the world through the vessels of the *sefiros*, and what would "blow the cover"?
How are the four Names spelled out, and what does the doubling of the letters in *BaN* say about *Malchus*?
What are the inside, middle and outside of a vessel, and how does the count of 248 limbs come out?
What are the two things that happen when the soul's power of sight goes into the eye?
How does designing a cup show that the vessel is made from the thickening of the light, and why do body and soul grow together until seventy?
